about.title: Rialto Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription:
Ten people died on Rialto's roads in 2025, according to the most recent final crash records. Behind each of those numbers is a household in San Bernardino County trying to make sense of an empty chair. If your family is one of them, please know there is no rush to read every word here. Take what you need.

A wrongful death claim in California is a civil action. It runs separately from any criminal case, and it can move forward even if no charges were ever filed. The law allows a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children to bring the claim first, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in other situations. Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance.

Rialto collisions cluster along Riverside Avenue, Baseline Road, SR-210, and Foothill Boulevard, and Friday afternoons see the most reports. Wherever and however your loss happened, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Rialto Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children before certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out who in your family is eligible so the claim is filed correctly the first time.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity such as the city or county is involved. Connecting sooner gives your attorney time to preserve evidence and meet every cutoff.

items.title: Free to you, contingency for the attorney
items.desc: LawProactive charges nothing for the connection, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Your family should not have to weigh legal costs against grief.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on Riverside Avenue and the police report is still pending. Can we start now?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death claim is a civil matter that does not have to wait for the Rialto Police Department or the CHP to finish their investigation, or for any criminal case to conclude. In fact, starting early lets an attorney request records, locate witnesses, and preserve evidence along the corridor before it disappears. Waiting for the criminal side can quietly eat into your two-year filing window.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law gives first priority to the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children of the person who died. If there is no one in that group, certain dependents and heirs may be able to file instead. Because families are complicated, an attorney can review your specific situation and explain who qualifies.

items.question: What losses can our family actually recover?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial costs and the financial support your loved one would have contributed over their expected lifetime. It also recognizes the loss of love, companionship, comfort, and guidance, which is often the largest part of a family's loss. No attorney can promise a particular result, but they can explain how these categories apply to your case.
